title: The Windkessel model of the circulation
description: The two-element Windkessel model. The heart pumps blood into the aorta in pulses (a flow source, 75 beats a minute, about 70 mL a beat); the aortic valve lets it through one way only. The elastic arteries store blood as they stretch (a compliance, 1 mL/mmHg) and the arterioles resist its flow out to the tissues (the peripheral resistance, 1.1 mmHg·s/mL). Run it: the aortic pressure swings between about 75 mmHg (diastolic) and 125 mmHg (systolic), and blood keeps flowing to the tissues between beats – smoothed, though it still rises and falls with each beat – even though the heart pumps in bursts. Make the arteries stiffer (lower the compliance) and watch the pulse pressure grow.
